data.text: Hong Kong's financial and technology selloff leaves Japan uneven, with banks and property already weak and technology still firmer.
Nikkei 225 fell 0.94% on the day but is still up 3.01% over one month, so the Hang Seng week is not a Japan index break.
USD/JPY last printed 157.83, down 0.06% on the day and up 1.39% over one month, so the yen has not strengthened as a haven.
Japan financials are down 3.7% over one month as a global bond sell-off drove borrowing costs higher.
Property is the weakest local sector, down 6.34% over one month, with 20-day volatility of 22.69%.
Technology is up 7.19% over one month, but 20-day volatility of 47.24% leaves that strength fragile to the Hang Seng technology rout.
Challenge to CHAIR: A neutral Japan Financials view conflicts with the 3.7% one-month decline and bond-selloff borrowing-cost pressure in local data.
Challenge to SPILLOVER: A bullish Japan Technology view is not supported; the Hang Seng technology rout and 47.24% local technology volatility argue for caution, not a lift.

data.plain_english: Hong Kong's stock market had a rough week, led by big banks and technology companies, while interest rates on US government debt climbed to their highest level in many years. The council expects Hong Kong shares, and banks and property companies in the US and Japan, to be more likely to fall, because higher borrowing costs tend to hurt these businesses. Mainland China looks more mixed, partly because its markets were closed on holiday during the drop. The council is most divided on US technology companies, which have risen recently but could be hurt if interest rates keep climbing. This is research to help you think, not advice to buy or sell anything.
